payload.reason: The evidence indicates that in the UCCA scheme, a node can represent either a terminal or a non-terminal, but not both simultaneously, as it is defined as either a single token or a complex unit comprising multiple tokens.

claims.text: A node in the UCCA scheme can be either a terminal or a non-terminal, but not both at the same time.
UCCA nodes are defined as either corresponding to a single token (terminal) or to multiple tokens viewed as a single entity (non-terminal).
